task_name: `GET /coordinating-session`, and the restart that resumes or says it cannot

rubric.result: The objective promises four things and each one is in the diff. (a) 'recalls the recorded conversation at start-up': ct-api.ts constructs RecoverCoordinatingSession with claudeConversations/sessionHooks/conversationRecords and calls execute() after server.start(), and the use case opens with `const conversation = await this.records.recall()`. (b) 'resumes it when Claude Code still holds it': `if (!this.conversations.isResumable(conversation)) ...` then `await this.sessionHooks.install(conversation.root)` and `const session = this.conversations.resume(conversation)`, returning CoordinatingSessionRecovered.live; ct-api then remembers it as CoordinatingSessionState.LIVE with SessionAttention.working(). (c) 'opens nothing when it does not': the unresumable branch returns before install/resume and never reaches start(); ClaudeConversations.resume/start are the only two openers and neither is called. (d) 'the page can read which of the three it is': CoordinatingSessionRoute.reading is registered as app.get on CoordinatingSessionRoute.PATH in api-server.ts, ahead of the app.all refusal, and answers none/live/unresumable with 200. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The TDD line asks for `it('opens nothing when Claude Code no longer holds the recorded conversation')` with the conversations double answering false to isResumable, asserting the outcome is unresumable AND that neither resume nor start was asked. The test in the diff is exactly that: `new Flow({ resumable: false })` drives ConversationsDouble.isResumable() to return false, then asserts `recovered.outcome` toBe RecoveredConversation.UNRESUMABLE, `flow.conversations.resumed` toEqual [] and `flow.conversations.started` toBe 0 — same assertion, same input, same expected value — and adds `flow.sessionHooks.installed` toEqual [], so the case really proves nothing was started, resumed or installed rather than only pinning the outcome string. The double reinforces it: start() throws 'RecoverCoordinatingSession must never call conversations.start'. The second named test, `it('resumes the recorded conversation instead of opening a new one')`, is present and asserts LIVE plus started toBe 0.

Compared name by name. RecoveredConversation is frozen with NONE:'none', LIVE:'live', UNRESUMABLE:'unresumable'. CoordinatingSessionRecovered declares outcome, conversation: CoordinatingConversation | null, session: LiveSession | null, in that order. RecoverCoordinatingSession takes `{ conversations, sessionHooks, records }` by name and `async execute(): Promise<CoordinatingSessionRecovered>`. CoordinatingSessionRoute.reading(held: CoordinatingSessions): RequestHandler answers 200 with {"status":"none"}, with {status:'live',conversation,repo,root,session:{id,name},attention:{status,question}} and with {status:'unresumable',conversation,repo,root,detail} — the three shapes the brief writes, keys included. ct-api.ts runs the recovery after server.start() (listeningPort is assigned first, which is what the hooks url closure reads) and writes one stderr line in each of the three cases. One deliberate narrowing: the brief writes `readonly outcome: string` and the diff writes `readonly outcome: RecoveredConversationValue`. That is the same field with a tighter type, and it is what conventions/defects.md demands ('A value that classifies something is a member of a closed vocabulary, not a string compared by hand'), so it is not a divergence I hold against the diff.

Row by row against the diff. D-21 is the row this task implements and it implements the stated value: a backend restart brings the conversation back by resuming it, a conversation that cannot be resumed is said out loud (status 'unresumable' with its detail, plus the stderr line 'claude code no longer holds it, nothing was resumed'), and the cabin is never handed a different conversation presented as the same — resume() is the only opener called and start() is never reached. D-25 holds: the resume path hands over no text at all (ClaudeConversations.resume passes `extra: {}`; only the start path carries CT_PHASE_PROMPT, and it is a path). D-10: every file added or modified is .ts. D-16: no new module names cmux and no new test needs it. D-13: nothing phase-like is stored; recovery derives its answer from the record plus what Claude Code still holds. D-18, D-22, D-26, D-1, D-11 and the button literal row are untouched by this diff, which complies by leaving them alone. No row is reopened.

conventions/defects.md, its four rules answered one by one. (1) Closed vocabulary: RecoveredConversation is a frozen vocabulary with its value type, and both dispatches over it — CoordinatingSessionRoute.#answerHolding and CtApi.#rememberCoordinatingSession — are switches whose default branch is `const exhaustive: never = ...` and a throw, so a new member fails at typecheck, which is what the document allows ('at compile time or by the type checker'). No loose string, no boolean standing in. One tension I declare instead of reporting: the route's 'none' comes from `held.held() === null` rather than from a member of CoordinatingSessionState, which is the document's 'An absent state is a member of the vocabulary, not an optional' — but coordinating-sessions.ts is not in this task's **Files:**, so adding the member was out of scope and the brief's Contract pins `{"status":"none"}` on exactly that null. (2) Raw map as the return value of logic: none. The use case returns the frozen value object CoordinatingSessionRecovered; the only maps are the object literals handed to Answer.send at the wire, one step before serialization, which is what the neighbouring `opening()` already does. (3) Two fields that have to agree: present, and declared rather than reported. CoordinatingSessionRecovered carries outcome alongside conversation|null and session|null, so 'LIVE with a null session' stays representable and the consumer reads it with `recovered.conversation!` / `recovered.session!`. That shape is dictated verbatim by the brief's Contract block, and HeldCoordinatingSession (task 7, not in **Files:**) already carries it; the implementer could not satisfy both the Contract and this rule, so the defect is in the plan. (4) Errors named for what happens: no new error type is introduced; the two throws are exhaustiveness guards named for what happens ('no coordinating session answer declared for ...'). Exemplars: the new application test reproduces backend/__tests__/application/open-coordinating-session.test.ts exactly — port subclasses as doubles, a shared `steps` array to pin order, a Flow handed to the use case constructor; the route test reuses the file's RunningApi/Mother idiom and asserts the literal body through a real listening server, which is conventions/testing.md's controller row; the GET registration copies the app.get + Browsers.turnAwayForeign + app.all shape of every other endpoint in api-server.ts. Layers and boundaries: recover-coordinating-session.ts sits in application/actions, imports only domain ports and value objects, takes its dependencies through the constructor by name and declares its result object beside it (conventions/architecture.md, 'The shape of a use case'); the concrete adapters are picked only in ct-api.ts, which is conventions/boundaries.md's outer edge. Delivery: no document of either yardstick prescribes a shape of delivery for adding a read endpoint; the GET lands beside the POST and METHODS already advertised 'GET, POST', so nothing was left on an old path. Considered and not reported: the repo projects vocabularies outwards with the Projection type (start-plan-route.ts, and CoordinatingSessionRefusal in this very file) while the diff hand-writes two switches — the switch is exhaustive at compile time, which is the stronger guarantee defects.md asks for, so I take it as idiom and not a finding. One low finding is recorded below about the domain error that escapes the outer edge.

The only test file that existed before is backend/__tests__/infrastructure/coordinating-session-route.test.ts, and its only `-` line is the import `-import { CoordinatingSessions } from '../../src/infrastructure/coordinating-sessions.ts'`, rewritten into a three-symbol import of the same module. No assertion, case or test is removed, relaxed or rewritten: the six tests that were there (202 with the conversation, holds it live and working, the repo_list refusal, nothing-to-plan, the conversation-not-started collapse, the 405) survive with their bodies byte for byte, including `expect(response.headers.get('allow')).toBe('GET, POST')`, which this task now makes true instead of weakening. Measured, nothing weakened.

The promised behaviour lives in production code, not in scaffolding. The recall/resume/open-nothing decision is backend/src/application/actions/recover-coordinating-session.ts; isResumable really reads Claude Code's transcript (ClaudeConversations.isResumable via ClaudeCodeTranscript over ~/.claude) and recall really reads the record on disk (DiskConversationRecords.recall of coordinating-session/conversation.json); the three answers are produced by CoordinatingSessionRoute.#answerHolding and reach the wire through the GET registered in api-server.ts; the start-up wiring is real, in ct-api.ts. Revert those production lines and every new test falls over — the application tests cannot import the module and the route tests get 405 from app.all instead of 200. No behaviour is carried by a double, a fixture or a hard-coded expected value.

The six touched paths are the six the **Files:** line declares, and what was written inside them serves the task: the use case and its result object; the reading handler with its detail constant; one app.get registration; the start-up construction, the call after server.start() and the #rememberCoordinatingSession dispatch that the Contract asks for; and the two test files with exactly the seven test names the **Tests:** list enumerates, plus the Mother.live/Mother.unresumable/RunningApi.get helpers those tests need. Nothing in ### Out of scope is touched: plugin/skills/brainstorming is untouched, POST /start-plan and its use case and adapters are untouched, no gate, groom or dispatcher code appears, and Home's restore path is not deleted. The diff contains no hunk of the plan file, so there is no amendment to rule on.

Seven new tests, four in the application file and three in the route file. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no randomness, no sleep; the route tests listen on port 0 and fetch 127.0.0.1 on the port the server answered, and the application tests touch nothing outside memory. Isolated: each test builds its own Flow or its own CoordinatingSessions, the values shared through Mother are frozen value objects, and the only shared mutable state — RunningApi.#started — is drained by the existing afterEach. Verifies real behaviour: the application assertions are on what the use case returned and on what each port received (conventions/testing.md's 'the observable effect'), and the route assertions are on the status and the literal body through a real server, so none of them would survive reverting the production lines. I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and its testing-anti-patterns.md reference for the finer half: nothing there is contradicted — the doubles are injected port implementations rather than mocks asserted on for their own sake, no test-only method was added to a production class, and no mock replaces a side effect a test depends on. The one thing the skill's 'Good Tests' table would question, the 'and' in `answers the live conversation with its attention and its question`, is the test name the plan's **Tests:** list prescribes literally and that ct-step's control searched for, so I declare it rather than report it.

findings.what: The start-up recovery lets a domain error escape the outer edge. ConversationRecords.recall() is declared to throw ConversationNotRecorded when the record exists but cannot be read as a conversation (DiskConversationRecords.recall wraps the parse in exactly that error), and ct-api.ts awaits recoverCoordinatingSession.execute() with nothing around it, after the port has already been printed and the server is listening. A truncated or hand-edited coordinating-session/conversation.json therefore kills the whole backend at start-up with an unhandled rejection instead of a diagnosis on the error channel — and it takes every other endpoint with it. The neighbouring start-up recovery does not have this shape: WorktreePlans.inFlight() hands its failure back as data (wereListed/reason) for ActivePlanRecovery to read. I record this as low rather than block on it: the brief's Contract closes the vocabulary at none/live/unresumable and no sentence of the task asks for a fourth path, and conventions/simplicity.md says in as many words that a judgement asking for an addition does not discharge its burden of proof. It is information for the person reading the slice, not work to send back.
findings.evidence: conventions/boundaries.md, 'The outer edge of the program': "It translates the domain's errors into the vocabulary of whoever invoked the program ... in a program that ends it is the exit code, the result on the standard channel and the diagnosis on the error channel, always separate" — against ct-api.ts:544 `CtApi.#rememberCoordinatingSession(` / `await recoverCoordinatingSession.execute(), coordinatingSessions, (line) => process.stderr.write(line)`, reached from `await CtApi.run(process.argv.slice(2), process.env)` at module level.
